messages.subject: RHadoop not working: Java heap space error
messages.subject_clean: RHadoop not working: Java heap space error
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am trying to get RHadoop working on a Hadoop cluster.

This is a test cluster for development / proof of concept.
It has 5 nodes, virtualized in VMware.
The OS on all nodes is centos 6.4

To install R on Hadoop, I followed these instructions:
https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki

The following example analysis is constantly failing with a Java heap size error:

groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
tapply(groups, groups, length)
require('rmr2')
groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
groups = to.dfs(groups)
result = mapreduce(
    input = groups,
    map = function(k,v) keyval(v, 1),
    reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, length(vv)))
print(result())
print(from.dfs(result, to.data.frame=T))

The code above is from this repo:
https://github.com/hortonworks/HDP-Public-Utilities/tree/master/Installation/r#rhadoop-validation

Any help to get this solved would be very much appreciated!

Best,

Manuel

messages.body_plain:
Many thanks for the quick feedback and the link!

Meanwhile I would like to add some further information on software versions used, just in case:
* plyrmr_0.4.0.tar.gz
* rhdfs_1.0.8.tar.gz
* rmr2_3.2.0.tar.gz
* epel-release-6-8.noarch.rpm
* rstudio-server-0.98.1028-x86_64.rpm
* R 3.1.0 (2014-04-10)

Best,

Manuel

On Monday, September 1, 2014 7:11:38 PM UTC+2, Manuel wrote:

> Hello!
>
> I am trying to get RHadoop working on a Hadoop cluster.
>
> This is a test cluster for development / proof of concept.
> It has 5 nodes, virtualized in VMware.
> The OS on all nodes is centos 6.4
>
> To install R on Hadoop, I followed these instructions:
> https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki
>
> The following example analysis is constantly failing with a Java heap size error:
>
> groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
> tapply(groups, groups, length)
> require('rmr2')
> groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
> groups = to.dfs(groups)
> result = mapreduce(
>     input = groups,
>     map = function(k,v) keyval(v, 1),
>     reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, length(vv)))
> print(result())
> print(from.dfs(result, to.data.frame=T))
>
>
> The code above is from this repo:
> https://github.com/hortonworks/HDP-Public-Utilities/tree/master/Installation/r#rhadoop-validation
>
> Any help to get this solved would be very much appreciated!
>
> Best,

> Manuel

Can you do what you need to do on a small scale outside mapreduce, in console? That would be step one. Second, I would think about the input to the mapreduce job. Third, move the rhbase code inside the map function and see what happens.

Antonio

>

>

messages.body_plain:
For the record, this is not the logs, nor the type of logs that the debugging guide recommends to look for initially. In this case though I think you are onto something with this log. Until recently, I think the last version, we let Hadoop run at configuration defaults with rmr jobs. That doesn't work very well with YARN because containers are monitored for memory use and java is allocated most of the space and R is left with nothing. So we set up rmr2 to modify the configuration for each job as follows

$hadoop
$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.map.java.opts=-Xmx400M"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.reduce.java.opts=-Xmx400M"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.map.memory.mb=4096"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.reduce.memory.mb=4096"

The values  have been generated asking around and trying a few jobs. They may be in need of refinement or maybe it's impossible to set them in a way that covers most needs. In your specific case it appears that mapreduce.reduce.java.opts is set too low. I am not sure why 400M shouldn't be enough though, as you are running one of the standard examples. Anyway, let's push that higher and see if we get through the reduce phase, at least we will have learnt something. To do that, get the current confguration:

bp  = rmr.options("backend.parameters")

#change

bp$hadoop[2] = "mapreduce.reduce.java.opts=-Xmx800M"

#check
bp

#set

rmr.options(backend.parameters = bp)

#check

rmr.options("backend.parameters")

And rerun. If it goes through, you have a workaround and I have a clue to work from, at least. In alternative or combination, you could try to increase mapreduce.reduce.memory.mb following similar steps. Thanks

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
sapply is mostly intended for interactive use and it will perform conversions based on some internal oracle that knows best what the function should do. Maybe use lapply or vapply instead. I don't see anything wrong with the results, so you may have to tell me what you expected. Since the difference is in that paste call, I would look into sep and collapse args and see if you need one of those (just a guess here, sorry if you have already).

Antonio

What I expect is for each key, paste the corresponding value to all element in vector wm. Have you checked the debugging guide <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/user%3Ermr%3EDebugging-rmr-programs>? I always start developing on the local backend, with local input files. Then you could call debug(tfM.map), rerun your program and see what happens line by line. If i understand right, the paste is the only difference between working program and failing program. So it must be recycling happening there, then interacting with recycling in the keyval function. What else could it be? Finally, there is nothing like allowing me to run this program by myself. I have the relevant functions. I need the output of

dump(wm, stdout())
dump(tfM.map_out, stdout())

That way I should be able to run the reduce phase. Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject: rhdfs: Deserialization problem.
messages.subject_clean: rhdfs: Deserialization problem.
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am Andrés Gordo and I work with Hadoop system. In our company project we developed a R algorithm, it, makes all calcs and write on HDFS using rhdfs, more specifically, hdfs.write function.

hdfs.write function, serializes the content file by default. Is possible write on HDFS directly without serialize the file? We can create the file on local system and use hdfs.put for upload it to HDFS, but, it is not directly writing.

On the other hand, we are trying deserialize the R file using Java (for integrate Java and R we are using JRI and rJava), but all attempts are unsuccessful. Anyone know anything about this?

We are searching manuals, tutorials, information about rhdfs and all RHadoop components, we don't found anything, only the Official RHadoop GitHub, but the documentation is not available here. You have got some king of guidance documents?

Thank you very much.
Andrés Gordo.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
thanks for the reproducible code! I started a fresh R session loaded rmr2 and switched to the local backend

rmr.options(backend = "local")

then set to debug the reducer

debug(tfm.reduce)

and run the last MR job again. I don't know why anyone who can reproduce a problem on a small input wouldn't want to try this approach. Clearly I am not sending out the message in the right way, and not for lack of trying.
The first thing I noticed is that v1 is sometimes a matrix, sometimes a vector (key 1). That's what you get for using sapply. If you don't believe me, this is what uber-R programer Hadley Wickham, author of half of CRAN, has to say about it in his Advanced R book:  "sapply() is great for interactive use because it saves typing, but if you use it inside your functions you’ll get weird errors if you supply the wrong type of input."
Mixing matrix and vector output is not supported in rmr. Once you output one keyval with arg types T1 and T2, all the following ones should have the same type. For matrices and data.frames, also the number of columns should be the same, and also the type and name of columns for data frames. Try to make your reducer satisfy this and I think it will start working correctly.

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: [RHadoop:#1651] Run MapReduce with rHBase
messages.body_plain:
I talked with people closely involved in the design of rhbse and they warned me that rhbase interfaces with hbase through a thrift server which could quickly become a bottleneck unless you make sure that each map process talks to a different thrift server, or to one of a large enough pool. If you followed the installation instruction node by node, then you'd have a thrift server running on each node and that should be scalable.

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
There is this document <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/user%3Ermr%3EEfficient-rmr-techniques> but it misses on some things, I need to update it. But it's useful. The biggest omission is that when you are confronted with small reduce groups, you have the option of a vectorized reduce, as long as you can reduce multiple groups efficiently (that is, not with an lapply over the groups). Other than that I don't see anything on the fly, but I marked this document for review. If you can share some use cases, it would be a service to the community to discuss them and they may even suggest improvements in rmr2 itself. Building plyrmr on top of rmr2 was alone the biggest driver behind rmr2 3.0 because of the use cases it suggested.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: rhdfs: Deserialization problem.
messages.subject_clean: rhdfs: Deserialization problem.
messages.body_plain:
You can't avoid serialization, by definition. From wikipedia:
>
> In computer science <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science>, in the context of data storage, serialization is the process of translating data structures <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_structure> orobject <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_(computer_science)> state into a format that can be stored (for example, in a file <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_file> or memory buffer <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_buffer>, or transmitted across anetwork <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_network> connection link) and reconstructed later in the same or another computer environment.[ <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serialization#cite_note-1>

What you need is a serialization format that's implemented on both sides.  I can't help with that, but once you have that settled, then read the manual for hdfs.write

> If the object is a raw vector, it is written directly to the con object, otherwise it is serialized and the bytes written to the con.

Antonio

messages.subject: How to be a more helpful group member
messages.subject_clean: How to be a more helpful group member
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rhadooopers
we are trying to apply a little bit of process to the management of this group so that we are more effective in answering. To help us doing that I would like to ask you a few things

Don't reuse old threads. New problem, new thread. If you think there is a thread that's related to your question, link to it, by all means.
Use the "Mark best answer" feature when appropriate. To us it means go straight to the next user, next problem. It saves a lot of time. Particularly, I am talking about the original poster, who is the only one who can mark the best answer (excluding moderators) to the best of my understanding. If your problem is solved, please let us move on as well. A little report on how thing went would be nice, but it takes time. A click, that's all we are asking. You can imagine how this workflow is incompatible with thread reuse, a.k.a thread hijacking.
Tag sensibly. Applying the maximum allowed number of tags just because you can is not sensible. Your question will not be prioritized.

As always, reproducible test cases of the type that can be simply cut and paste into an R vanilla session is the best way to get answers. Thanks!

Antonio

I am a novice user of R and I am in the process of installing RHadoop single node cluster on Ubuntu 14.04LTS. If any of you could point me to some documentation with steps for installation it would be really helpful. I tried searching for the same in the group but some of the links pointed where no more available also I would wanted to confirm if the steps are the same for RHadoop single node cluster? Please help.

Thanks in advance

I did a fork of avro and I've been working on a new branch of the release 1.7.4 which is the version that I'm running and I got the "ravro:::avro_get_schema" working fine with files from HDFS.

Now I'm facing problems with the next steps. Considering the following code, I did some changes to use "rhdfs:::hdfs.line.reader" instead of "readLine".

avro.input.format = function(schema.file, ..., read.size = 10^5) {
 schema = ravro:::avro_get_schema(file = schema.file)
 function(con) {
   lines = readLines(con = con, n = read.size)
   if (length(lines) == 0)
     NULL
   else {
     x = splat(paste.fromJSON)(lines)
     y = ravro:::parse_avro(x, schema, encoded_unions=FALSE, ...)
     keyval(NULL, y)
   }
 }
}

I'm stuck in the line "x = splat(paste.fromJSON)(lines)".

The first problem that I found is the function "splat" which is not defined. Doing a search on github I found this code https://github.com/hadley/plyr/blob/master/R/splat.r but I'm not sure if this function is supposed to be used here.

The second point that I perceived is that the function "paste.fromJSON" is not defined, so I took a look at "rjson" library and I found only "fromJSON".

Yes, I can do it but first of all I need to do a refactoring in order to correct things that I simplified in my test code.

Regarding to the avro I had to patch 1.7.4 cause it's the version that is running on my cluster due to CDH 4.7. I believe that it won't be a problem since I can backport the patch that you mentioned.

Renan

Hello,

I am looking for any pointers or guidance on the make.input.format function.  I am attempting to read a gzip file in the map phase and attempting to use the make.input.format to setup the input correctly for mapreduce.  I am using -D options we use for Java Streaming, namely:

-D mapred.output.compression.codec=org.apache.hadoop.io.compress.GzipCode \

-D mapred.output.compress=true \
Here is my sample code.  When I run this, I never get the stderr output and I quickly get a "Error: Java heap space" in the console.  The file I am reading is fairly large.

Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/local/bin/hadoop")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/usr/local/Cellar/hadoop/2.5.0/libexec/share/hadoop/tools/lib/hadoop-streaming-2.5.0.jar")

library(rhdfs)
hdfs.init()
library(rmr2)

json_reducer <- function(name, counts) {
  keyval(name, sum(counts))}

json_mapper <- function(k, v)
{
  write(paste("Running Mapper"), stderr())
  keyval("test", 1)
}

custInput <- make.input.format(format = "native", mode = "binary", backend.parameters =
                                 list(D="mapred.input.compression.codec=org.apache.hadoop.io.compress.GzipCode",

messages.body_plain:
Hi Brian,
have you tried help(make.input.format)? First, you don't tell us what the format of your data is, besides that it is compressed.  I will assume json from the function names you are using. I see a couple of problems with your use of that function. If you specify format as a string, you are calling from predefined combination of the other options. It's the quick-and-easy. If you want full flexibility, you have to specify format as a function, then mode, streaming format and optionally backend parameters. Mix the two and you won't get what you expect. The other thing, native is not json.  I suspect you are sending json into the parser for typedbytes which is not the most resilient component ever written. That's probably where you get the heap space problem. We support json-ish with make.input.format("json"), but I call it json-ish because we need to have one json object per line and to have newlines and tabs escaped. That's how we made json fit with what hadoop streaming expects (on record per line, key and value separated by the first tab). So if you have any json that won't work. It's not the ideal level of json support, we accept suggestions on how to make it better. The missing piece is a json parser that can read one object from a connection. Right now we need to read x lines from stdin and pass them to the parser, which fails if the json object is not complete, hence the decision to put an object per line. Most people will need to preprocess their json before using this input, which is less than ideal. If you wanted to write your own input format, I would go about it as follows

true.json.format.fun = function(con){
 text = readLines(con, n = ...)
 obj = parse.json(text)
 keyval(NULL, obj)}

This is a function taking a connection as input and returning a key-val pair. What I don't know is the value for n or how to parse a partial json obj. Maybe you can make additional assumptions for your application, maybe you have a parser that can read from a connection or can develop one. Then you assemble the input format

true.json.input.format = make.input.format(format = true.json.format.fun, mode = "text", backend.parameters = <as you have them already>)

It would be nice to have a general json reader and replace the json-ish one we have now. Pull requests welcome.

Antonio

Antonio,

custInput <- make.input.format(format = "sequence.typedbytes")

Brian

Bind.cols can't work directly off to.dfs output. rmr2 and plyrmr have some interoperability, but you can't mix and match to your heart's content.

> Even I try with iris dataset it's work.
> How can i perform plyrmr or any mapreduce as a data set for csv file what I can do.
> Or do i have to make my csv file as a data set to deal with plyrmr.
> Some suggestion and guideline plz.

I would try to build a self-contained plyrmr example that I can run, for instance using the iris or mtcars data sets and learn each package before mixing and matching with rmr2. This works for me

bind.cols(input(iris), aspect = Sepal.Length/Sepal.Width)

This also works (shows how to read from disk after creating on-disk data set)

IF = make.input.format("csv",sep = ",",stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
OF = make.output.format("csv",sep = ",")
iris.on.disk = output(input(iris), format = OF, input.format = IF)
bind.cols(input(iris.on.disk), aspect = Sepal.Length/Sepal.Width)

If you replace iris.on.disk with a path to an existing data set in the same format, it should also work.

Sorry again, while a package is in 0.x.x release backward compatibility requirements are waived or at least relaxed (see semver.org <http://semver.org> for details). I would suggest reading help(count) and see if that gets you going.

>

count(mtcars, carb:cyl, carb:gear)

So it's a lot more flexible than count.cols, but you need to give it additional arguments. I don't have 0.4.0 installed right now, but I hope there is a help(count) entry that tells you as much. If you are disappointed that we had a backward incompatible change, you'd be better off waiting for a 1.0 release, but I don't have a timetable for that. What we are doing right now is making an early release available to get feedback and develop based on what people do with it or not.
